identity.title: Scaling In-the-Wild Training for Diffusion-based Illumination Harmonization and Editing by Imposing Consistent Light Transport

problem.claim: Scale diffusion-based illumination editing to varied, in-the-wild data while preserving image details and intrinsic properties such as albedo.

gap.claim: Direct training on complex, varied data lacks constraints that reliably separate illumination manipulation from unintended structural or material changes.

contributions.claim: IC-Light imposes consistent light transport during training using a physical linear-blending principle for mixed illumination.
The method supports training across more than 10 million examples, multiple data sources, and strong backbones including SDXL and Flux.
The approach is designed to modify illumination while preserving other intrinsic image properties.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by imposing consistent light transport as a physically grounded training constraint for scalable illumination learning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report scaling illumination-editing training to more than 10 million examples spanning real light stages, rendered samples, and in-the-wild synthetic augmentations.
The authors report reduced uncertainty and mitigation of artifacts including mismatched materials and altered albedos.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion models are positioned as useful for illumination harmonization and editing, but scaling training risks loss of details and intrinsic properties.
Without suitable constraints, training on varied in-the-wild data may yield a structure-guided random image generator instead of precise illumination manipulation.
IC-Light imposes consistent light transport based on linear blending across illumination conditions.
The authors report large-scale, multi-source training and fewer uncertainties or material/albedo artifacts.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a physical consistency principle directly to scalable training, intrinsic-property preservation, and artifact mitigation.

lessons.interpretation: A domain-grounded constraint can serve simultaneously as the method’s rationale and as a bridge between the intended behavior and reported outcomes.
lessons.application: When proposing a controllable generative system, state a task-specific invariant and map it explicitly to the failure mode and claimed behavioral evidence.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when no defensible domain invariant exists or when the proposed constraint cannot be connected to observable outcomes.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative metrics, baselines, ablations, or experimental conditions for the reported reductions and artifact mitigation.
It does not specify how preservation of intrinsic properties is measured or whether all listed backbones and data types were evaluated under comparable settings.
